newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa sinks to six month low, volume active.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa sinks to six month low, volume active.

text.p: London cocoa futures, pressured by trade profit-taking and speculative selling, sank to a six-month low, ending the day barely above the nadir.
But traders said the market was poised for an upward technical correction after finishing lower for seven or eight successive sessions.
"The selling seems to be a bit overdone," said one trader.
Traders said some sell-stops emerged after the benchmark December broke through a widely-watched 965 stg support level early in the session.
It sank to a six-month low of 955 stg before settling 10 stg down at 957 stg. Other positions were down five to eight stg but just off the session's lows.
Traders said some light trade and industry buying on the dips emerged to help pare the losses.
Traders pegged immediate support at 945 stg basis December. The upside target is seen at 1,000.

Volume on the exchange was an impressive 10,312 lots, with crosses and switches accounting for 3,000 to 4,000 lots of the trades. March 1997/March 1998 switch was seen traded at 80 stg and May/May at 78.
